research_scope: Source-free mathematical prerequisite identity audit against original formulation text; parent scope and stronger structural conditions remain distinct.

aliases.reason: The tensor comparison in Mittag-Leffler modules uses ∏_i Q_i, the unrestricted product of a family of R-modules; the inverse-limit source uses an instance of this arbitrary product for a countable system. Coordinates, product operations and infinite supports agree. Tensor injectivity and inverse-limit compatibility remain separate parent constraints.

The rational absolute-value source and the strictly-positive-rational source each invoke the usual total order on Q, compatible with rational addition and multiplication by positive elements. The strict-positivity predicate and absolute-value piecewise formula are distinct parent definitions; their ordering prerequisite is identical.

The quasi-separated and separated morphism sources use the identical relative diagonal Δ_{X/S}:X→X×_S X, characterized by both compositions with fibre-product projections being id_X. Quasi-compactness of that diagonal and closed immersion of that diagonal are distinct additional hypotheses retained separately.

The K_0 source uses isomorphism classes of finite projective R-modules and the K'_0 source uses isomorphism classes of finitely generated R-modules. The common prerequisite is module isomorphism equivalence under invertible R-linear maps, restricted to different classes of modules in the source; no equality of those two K-groups follows.

The simple undirected graph and loopless undirected multigraph sources both describe an individual edge by an unordered two-element vertex subset {u,v} with u≠v. Multiplicity of those subsets in the multigraph, versus unique edge membership in the simple graph, is separately preserved in the parent definitions.
